clinician.final_diagnosis: fatal invasive osteomyelitis in an allo-HSCT recipient caused by RM
clinician.trajectory_summary: 73-year-old male allo-HSCT recipient (MDS-RAEB I, 6 months post-transplant on posaconazole prophylaxis) presented with critical septic condition featuring fever >40°C and dyspnea requiring intubation and mechanical ventilation. CT showed bilateral pulmonary infiltrates and lumbar spondylodiscitis was ruled out by MRI. Initial microbiologic investigations were negative and patient improved under empiric antibacterial, antiviral, and azole therapy. Subsequently developed right hip pain. Imaging (ultrasound, CT, MRI) revealed new bone infarct with massive secondary osteomyelitis involving the right femoral head, neck, and trochanteric region with cortical breakthrough into soft tissue (E004). Emergency surgical intervention demonstrated extensive bone and soft tissue destruction with ubiquitous blackened necrotic tissue characteristic of mucormycosis; proximal femoral resection was performed with placement of antibiotic (vancomycin, gentamycin, clindamycin) and amphotericin B-loaded spaceholder plus extensive debridement (E005). Microbiological and histopathological analysis with BLAST identification confirmed Rhizopus/Rhizomucor (RM) (E006). Despite maximal multimodal care including surgical debridement and local antifungal therapy, disease progression was drastic. Further therapeutic interventions were stopped with transition to palliative home care, and the patient died a few days later (E010).

MRI demonstrated new bone infarct with massive secondary osteomyelitis in right femoral head, neck, and trochanter with cortical breakthrough to soft tissue
Emergency surgery revealed extensive bone and soft tissue destruction with ubiquitous blackened tissue (pathognomonic for mucormycosis)
Proximal femoral resection performed with amphotericin B-loaded spaceholder and extensive debridement
Microbiological and histopathological analysis with BLAST identified Rhizopus/Rhizomucor (RM)
Fatal outcome with drastic disease progression under maximal multimodal care, transition to palliative care, and death within days
Patient was on posaconazole prophylaxis at presentation, representing breakthrough mucormycosis
